Lab 7

Venus flytrap

Investigate how mechanical stimulation becomes an electrical response and rapid plant movement. Compare contact patterns, collect evidence, and explain the ecological value of selective trapping.

8 activities100 points2 submissions
Learning objectives and lab workflow
  • Distinguish trigger hairs from marginal cilia and digestive glands.
  • Compare contact number, simulated timing and hair identity under controlled conditions.
  • Separate initial capture from sealing and digestive activation.
  • Support a scientific claim with recorded evidence and acknowledge model limitations.

Write a prediction first. Record each trial before Reset Trap or New Trial. Save your work before leaving. Completion checks identify missing work without revealing the grading key. Incorrect responses can still be submitted.

Images are generated botanical illustrations. The sequence uses compressed visual timing, not footage of a living plant. This model advances the experimental clock only with the time controls. It does not measure voltage or calcium. Closed-trap hairs remain visible schematically for post-capture stimulation.
